what_this_is: Ring R2 lane (b)'s IO-boundary contract model: every measured IO site in data/verdict_set.json's b_io_bearing partition, classified by EFFECT (what it does) and by DEPENDENCE (whether the verdict turns on the IO's content or only on its success), each effect class carrying the contract the verdict path assumes, what checks it today, and — where nothing does — a §3.6 assumption-ledger row with a probe. The ledger only shrinks. Nothing here is earned: this artifact models the obligation, it does not discharge it.

derivation.shared_denominator: the site scan is IMPORTED from scripts/verdict_set.py (production_lines + IO_TOKENS) and re-run over the same members at the same pinned digests; a total that disagrees with the committed io_site_total aborts the mint

axis_1_effect.what: what the site actually does, decided by ordered lexical rules over the LEXED line (comments and literals blanked, #[cfg(test)] mod bodies removed); first match wins; a site matching no rule aborts the mint

rules.means: a `use` item — the module names a type; no syscall is issued here
a TYPE position (error-enum field, `#[from]`, return type, closure/fn parameter) — `std::io::Error`, `Mmap` and `std::process::{ExitStatus,Output}` as types, not operations
an io::Error VALUE is constructed or inspected (`ErrorKind::…`, `Error::new`) — error plumbing, no syscall
an in-memory buffer wearing an IO name (`io::Cursor`, `MmapMut::map_anon`) — no file
a child process's stdin/stdout/stderr stream is read or written
a child process is configured or spawned (`Command::new`, `Stdio::…`)
a file's metadata is read without reading its content (`fs::metadata`)
a file or directory is created, written, appended, copied or removed

axis_2_dependence.what: whether the verdict's correctness depends on the IO's CONTENT or only on its SUCCESS — the axis that decides what a contract costs

classes.verdict-irrelevant: no syscall is issued at this site, so no verdict can turn on its result. These sites are IO-bearing only in the token scan; they cost nothing to contract, and their only residual assumption is that the LEXICAL classification is right (ledger row L-LEX).
classes.success-only: the verdict depends on whether the call SUCCEEDED, never on what came back — the bytes were computed in memory before the call. This is the cheap class: the contract is discharged by 'the error is propagated, and no partial artifact is later read as authoritative', with no pinning, no digest and no provenance chain.
classes.content-bearing: the verdict changes with what the IO RETURNED — the bytes, the entry set, the variable's value, the child's output. This is the expensive class: the contract can only be discharged by binding the returned value to something the verdict's provenance already pins.

derivation.reporting_only_extraction: spawned program names and environment-variable names are read from the RAW line (literals intact) to NAME what is spawned or read. They feed no classification decision — every classification rule above runs on the lexed line, per gate-registry R9.
fail_closed: source artifact absent / malformed / wrong schema
a lane (b) member file is absent, or its sha256 has drifted from the pinned one
the re-derived site total disagrees with the committed io_site_total
any site matches no effect rule
an effect class with measured sites has no contract
a cited check or hole no longer resolves in the tree
a ledger row lacks statement, probe, discharge, date or owning job
the ledger row count grows without --rebase-up
derivation.regenerate: scripts/verdict_io_contracts.py     (--check to verify the committed file)

declaration_only_members.what: members whose every IO token hit is a declaration / error value / in-memory buffer: they are IO-BEARING in the token scan and issue no IO at all. This is the measured half of lane (b)'s 'decode-pure separated from read-IO' obligation that needs no refactor — the split is already there, it had just never been measured.

contracts.title: the bytes read are the bytes the verdict was minted over
contracts.statement: Every byte a verdict path consumes from a file is the byte its provenance was established over: the path names the file that was digested, the file is not substituted between the pin and the read, and a short or truncated read is refused rather than decoded.

checked_by.what: the EAGER shard readers (`ShardReader::from_bytes`, `ShardMmapReader::from_mmap`) recompute a whole-file blake3 and compare it to the footer, so on those two entry points corruption and truncation are caught

holes.what: `open_lazy` / `open_lazy_from_bytes` route through a reader that SKIPS the footer blake3 by design (demand paging: checking it would fault every page), so on the lazy path nothing verifies the bytes at all
the KernelVerified manifest is read back as authoritative JSON with no digest, no signature and no comparison to the run that wrote it

contracts.why_unproved: the footer digest travels INSIDE the file it certifies, so it detects corruption, not substitution; and the twelve members outside clean-mathverse's shard path read their inputs with no integrity check of any kind.
contracts.discharge: bind every content-bearing read to a digest the verdict's provenance already pins (the shard footer for shards; an artifact-lineage digest for manifests), and require the checksummed reader on any path that will MINT a verdict.

contracts.title: the enumerated entry set is the input set the verdict quantifies over
contracts.statement: A directory walk returns exactly the input set the verdict quantifies over: no entry appears or disappears during the walk, no entry is silently dropped for being a symlink, non-UTF-8 or unreadable, and enumeration order does not change the verdict.

holes.what: an unreadable directory is indistinguishable from an EMPTY one here: the `Err` arm is dropped, so 'nothing to verify' and 'could not look' produce the same verdict

contracts.why_unproved: nothing in lane (b) pins the entry set: no manifest lists the files a walk is expected to find, so a walk that returns a subset produces a verdict over a subset and says so nowhere.
contracts.discharge: quantify every walk over a committed manifest and refuse on set difference in BOTH directions (missing and unexpected), rather than over whatever the filesystem returned.

contracts.title: equal metadata implies equal content
contracts.statement: When a cache returns a previously parsed module because the file's mtime equals the recorded mtime, the file's CONTENT equals the content that was parsed.

holes.what: the module cache's hit condition IS the assumption: mtime equality is taken as content equality, and the hit returns an `Arc<ParsedModule>` that later feeds registration

contracts.why_unproved: mtime equality does not imply content equality — a same-second rewrite, an archive restore, a `touch -r`, or a coarse-granularity filesystem all produce equal mtimes over different bytes. (One direction IS fail-closed: a failed `stat` yields `None`, and the hit condition requires `is_some()`, so a stat failure misses rather than falsely hits.)
contracts.discharge: key the cache on something that implies content equality — at minimum `(len, mtime_ns, dev, ino)` from the stat already being made, and a content digest on any path whose output is used to MINT a verdict rather than to serve a query.

contracts.title: no environment variable can weaken a verdict
contracts.statement: The ABSENCE of every environment variable is the safe default, and no value a caller can set either changes what a verdict depends on or escapes being recorded in that verdict's provenance.

holes.what: a BEHAVIOUR-CHANGING variable on an import path: default ON, and `=0` turns the Coq `Var` universe re-leveling arm off — two runs of the same input under different environments are two different programs
a BEHAVIOUR-CHANGING variable: `MATHVERSE_MAX_DECOMPRESS_BYTES` moves the decompression bound a shard read is refused at

contracts.why_unproved: nothing enumerates these reads or pins their dispositions. In particular `data/env_bypass_census.json` + `scripts/check_env_bypass_census.py` do NOT cover them despite the name: that census watches the kernel `Environment` bypass surface (`extend_*_unchecked`, `add_decl_structural`), not `std::env` reads. Reading the name as coverage is the exact mistake this row exists to prevent.
contracts.discharge: commit a table of every variable name lane (b) reads with a declared disposition (`diagnostic-only` / `behaviour-changing`), enforce it here so an unlisted name aborts the mint, and require every behaviour-changing name to appear in the provenance of any verdict minted under it.

contracts.title: the spawned process is the pinned binary
contracts.statement: A spawned program is the pinned binary at the pinned version: the name resolves to one intended executable rather than the first PATH match, and the executable that actually ran is the one whose identity the verdict's provenance records.

checked_by.what: `capture_solver_binary` RECORDS a spawned solver's `--version` output and the sha256 of its executable — the identity is measured, which is half the contract

holes.what: the version spawn and the digest read are two SEPARATE resolutions of `spec.path`, and the recorded digest is compared to no pin — a fingerprint is provenance, not a gate

contracts.why_unproved: 17 of the 23 spawn sites pass a BARE NAME resolved through `PATH` (`tar` x6, `gh` x4, `git` x3, `zstd` x2, `date`, `gzip`), 3 pass a caller-supplied path or variable, and 3 only configure stdio for a spawn started on another line — see this row's `spawned_programs` / `program_resolution` tallies, which are derived, not typed. Nothing resolves a bare name to an absolute path, records which executable answered, or compares it to anything. This is also where the network enters the surface: `std::net` has ZERO direct sites in lane (b), but `gh` is a network client spawned from the release/artifact path, so 'no sockets' is not 'no network'.
contracts.discharge: resolve each tool once to an absolute path, fingerprint it through the `capture_solver_binary` machinery that already exists, and compare the digest to a committed pin before the first spawn.

contracts.title: a child's output is consumed faithfully, and never rounds up to a pass
contracts.statement: A child process's verdict-bearing output is consumed faithfully: a non-zero exit, a killed or timed-out child, a truncated stream, or a short response is an error or an explicit non-pass — never silently a pass.

checked_by.what: a non-zero exit becomes `CheckerError::Exit` carrying the code and stderr, not a verdict
a child that outruns its deadline is killed and every obligation in the batch becomes `Timeout` — the timeout path cannot produce a pass
a short response is a protocol error, so verdicts cannot silently be re-indexed onto the wrong obligations

holes.what: both streams are drained AFTER `child.wait()`, so a child that fills the pipe buffer blocks on write while the parent blocks on wait — a LIVENESS hazard (hang), not a soundness one, and worth separating from the rest of this row

contracts.why_unproved: the three checks cover how a FAILING child is reported; what they do not cover is the succeeding one — the checker's `Proved` verdicts are trusted by construction and are re-checked by nothing, so this contract's soundness rests entirely on whether the external program is in the TCB.
contracts.discharge: either declare the external checker TCB with a pinned digest (C-SPAWN-IDENTITY) and say so in the trust register, or require every accepted verdict to carry a certificate the Clean kernel re-checks — the S&L §0.6 'diverse re-check' posture.

contracts.title: ambient process state is a nonce, never a verdict input
contracts.statement: `std::process::id()` is used only for uniqueness, so two runs over the same input that differ only in pid produce the same verdict.

holes.what: the pid is hashed INTO an attempt identifier, so the identifier is not reproducible across runs — benign for a nonce, load-bearing if an identifier is ever compared

contracts.why_unproved: the nonce reading is by inspection of two sites; nothing enforces that a third site cannot let the pid reach a verdict.
contracts.discharge: a determinism probe — mint the same verdict twice in one tree and diff — plus this enumeration held at exactly two sites by the gate.

contracts.title: a write lands completely or reports an error (the CHEAP class)
contracts.statement: Every write either lands completely or reports an error; no partially written artifact is later read back as authoritative. The write's CONTENT needs no contract at all — the bytes were computed in memory before the call, so the verdict depends on the call's SUCCESS and on nothing that came back.

checked_by.what: one record writer refuses to clobber an existing file (`create_new`), so a re-run cannot silently overwrite the record a previous verdict was minted against

holes.what: `fs::write` is not atomic: a crash or a full disk mid-write leaves a truncated JSON manifest that `from_file` will later read as authoritative
the error is DISCARDED, so 'or reports an error' is simply false at this site and the two others shaped like it

contracts.why_unproved: no write in lane (b) is atomic — nothing writes to a temporary and renames, though `scripts/verdict_set.py` does exactly that two directories away — and several sites drop the error entirely.
contracts.discharge: tmp-write + rename for the writes whose output is read back as authoritative, and propagate (or explicitly justify discarding) every write error. This is the cheapest class in the model and should close first.

measured_absent.title: no verdict path opens a socket directly
measured_absent.statement: No member of lane (b) constructs a `std::net` socket type.
measured_absent.caveat: This is NOT 'lane (b) does not reach the network'. `gh` — the GitHub CLI, a network client — is spawned at four sites in `artifacts.rs` and `release.rs`. Network reachability lives in C-SPAWN-IDENTITY, not here.

residue_class.title: token hits that issue no syscall
residue_class.statement: These sites matched the IO token table but perform no IO: they import a module, name a type, construct or inspect an `io::Error` value, or wrap an in-memory buffer in an IO-shaped API. No verdict can turn on their result, so no contract is owed.

ledger.what: the §3.6 assumption ledger for lane (b): one row per (contract x member) that nothing fully checks, plus the rows this MODEL itself stands on. Each row carries a statement, a probe command, a discharge condition, a date and an owning job.
ledger.destination: data/spine_assumption_ledger.json, when that file exists; until then these rows live here and scripts/verdict_gate.sh reads them from here

row_ratchet.what: assumption-ledger rows; may fall freely, may rise only through scripts/verdict_io_contracts.py --rebase-up '<reason>' (recorded below)

rows.statement: The effect classification is LEXICAL: a site's class is decided from the single matched line, not from the program's semantics. Every site classified declaration-import / declaration-type / error-value / in-memory-no-io is asserted to issue no syscall on that evidence alone — a macro expansion, a type alias, or a `Deref` impl could hide an operation the matched line does not show.
rows.discharge: re-derive the classification from MIR/THIR rather than from source lines — the same whole-crate dump G-SPINE-SET waits on (data/spine_set.PENDING.md).

rows.statement: The site denominator is the IO_TOKENS table in scripts/verdict_set.py, so it is a LOWER bound on lane (b)'s IO surface: an IO call reached through an in-crate helper, through a dependency's API (`serde_json::from_reader`, `zstd::decode_all`, an HTTP client), or through a macro is not a site. The counts in this artifact are what that table can SEE, not what the surface does.
rows.probe: scripts/verdict_io_contracts.py --describe   # prints the borrowed token table
rows.discharge: derive sites from the call graph instead of from tokens; until then, every added token lands with a mutation arm proving the scan would have missed it before.

recommendations.cheap_because: the digest is ALREADY COMPUTED on the same code path and thrown at a report
recommendations.what: `capture_solver_binary` (crates/clean-mathverse/src/env_fingerprint.rs) already runs `spec.path --version` and computes `sha256_hex` over the executable's bytes. Nothing compares that digest to a pin. Add a committed pin table and one equality check before the first verdict-bearing spawn.
recommendations.cost: one committed table + one string comparison per solver per run; ZERO new IO (the read and the hash already happen). Add an absolute-path resolution to close the TOCTOU between the version spawn and the digest read.

recommendations.cheap_because: the digest exists in the file and the checked reader is already written
recommendations.what: `ShardMmapReader::from_mmap` verifies the whole-file blake3 footer; `open_lazy` routes around it through `from_mmap_no_checksum` for demand paging. Require the checksummed reader whenever the run will MINT a KernelVerified verdict, and keep the lazy reader for serving.
recommendations.cost: one full-file blake3 per shard per MINT run — and a mint run materializes every constant anyway, so the pages it would fault are pages it faults regardless. No new algorithm, no new dependency; a mode flag on the open path.

recommendations.cheap_because: the enumeration is already derived here; only the table is missing
recommendations.what: Commit the six variable names lane (b) reads with a declared disposition (diagnostic-only / behaviour-changing) and enforce it in THIS script, so an unlisted name aborts the mint and a diagnostic-only variable that grows teeth cannot do so silently.
recommendations.cost: ~40 lines here plus a 6-row table; ~0.3 s per gate run; NO crate change — this one is inside this lane's ownership and is the cheapest real close in the model.

recommendations.cheap_because: reuses capture_solver_binary, which already exists and is already called
recommendations.what: Resolve the six bare-name tools (`gh`, `tar`, `zstd`, `gzip`, `git`, `date`) once to absolute paths and fingerprint them through the existing solver-binary machinery, so the provenance of a release artifact names the executables that built it.
recommendations.cost: one PATH resolution + one read + one sha256 per tool per run (six tools). Note this is also where the network enters: `gh` is a network client and `std::net` shows zero sites.

recommendations.cheap_because: the pattern is already written two directories away, in verdict_set.py
recommendations.what: The two JSON artifacts that are written and later read back as authoritative — `kernel_verified_manifest.rs` (`fs::write` then `from_file`) and `release.rs` (`fs::write` then `read_to_string`) — should write to a temporary and rename, exactly as `scripts/verdict_set.py` does (`tmp.write_text(...); tmp.replace(out)`).
recommendations.cost: two extra lines per site and one rename syscall; removes the torn-artifact hole for precisely the writes whose output is read back.

recommendations.cheap_because: PARTLY — the cheap variant is free, the sound variant is not
recommendations.what: clean-olean's module cache keys on mtime alone. The FREE improvement is to key on `(len, mtime_ns, dev, ino)` from the `fs::metadata` call already being made, which closes the same-second rewrite and the archive-restore cases. The SOUND fix — a content digest — is NOT cheap and should be stated as such: it means reading the file the cache exists to avoid reading, so it belongs on mint paths only, never on the serve path.
recommendations.cost: cheap variant: zero new syscalls, a wider key struct. Sound variant: one full read + hash per cache probe — quote it honestly rather than calling the whole row cheap.
